answer: Treat the ledger like a lighthouse on a knoll above an ocean of keys: it lights passing hulls, not flags. Each epoch the protocol posts a bounded queue of paid microtasks, ordered by a public beacon. An identity claims work by revealing a nullifier derived from its key, so each task instance is consumed once. A thousand minted keys buy a thousand empty queues: only peer-verified output earns standing; clones that claim without delivering earn nothing. An attacker pays continuous compute and forfeits rewards on every fake, so cost scales with delivered work, not registration speed.
